appropriate: a pill outline holding a bar, a dot and a D-shape reads as a toggle switch or capsule; the ledger and 'where you stand' need a paragraph

no competitor uses a capsule, but a filled disc inside a rounded frame sits close to the category's letter-in-a-circle and the banned coin
simple: one capsule outline with three inner parts; drawable with effort, the inner parts compete
pill outline, disc and two flanking bars are three competing parts; redrawable with effort
legible: the capsule holds to 32 px; at 24 and 16 px the inner bars and dot fill in to a dark lozenge
at 24 and 16 px the mark collapses to a chain-link or infinity glyph; the serif wordmark reads well in the header
adaptable: works in one colour and reversed, but in the app tile it is a small wide shape floating in a square and the avatar is tiny
black, reversed and one-colour panels hold, but the wide capsule shrinks to a thin sliver inside the square app tile
timeless: rounded pill UI shapes are a current product-design look; not on the avoid list but dated to app-era interfaces
no trend shape from trends.md; plain geometric capsule
universal: rotated 90 reads as a traffic light or a pill/figure; horizontal it reads as a toggle or a chain link
rotated 90 it reads as a traffic light or medicine capsule; mirrored is unchanged
clear: unsearched: toggle and capsule marks are common across fintech and SaaS apps
unsearched: resembles the generic UI toggle-switch glyph and pill/capsule pharmacy marks seen widely
congruent: round, horizontal pill contradicts the page-like framed ledger, the softened-but-angular shape target and the front-vowel light mark; static and simple match
round, heavy and disc-centred where the targets ask for level ruled forms at medium weight; the disc echoes the forbidden coin
system: lockups and tiers built, but the wide aspect wastes the app tile and favicon
lockups, tiers and icon all built from the one capsule, but the icon and favicon are under-scaled and the 16 px tier is not redrawn
